[[File:Filip Rindler Oberwolfach 2026.jpg|thumb|Rindler at [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2026]]
'''Filip Rindler''' (born August 15, 1984 in [[Berlin]]) is an [[Austria|Austrian]] [[mathematician]]. After studying at [[Technische Universität Berlin|TU Berlin]], he finished his doctorate at the [[University of Oxford]] in 2011 under the supervision of [[Jan Kristensen]]. Since 2020 he is a Professor at the [[University of Warwick]]. He works on [[Calculus of variations|the calculus of variations]], [[Partial differential equation|partial differential equations]] and [[geometric measure theory]], as well as mathematical material science.

In 2018 he was awarded the prestigious [[Whitehead Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]] for "his solutions to fundamental problems on the border between the theory of partial differential equations, calculus of variations and geometric measure theory".<ref>{{Cite web |title=2018 LMS Prize Winners {{!}} London Mathematical Society |url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/news-entry/29062018-1745/2018-lms-prize-winners |access-date=2024-08-24 |website=www.lms.ac.uk}}</ref> He received an [[European Research Council|ERC]] Starting Grant in 2017<ref name=":0">{{cite web|access-date=2022-09-20 |title=Datahub of ERC funded projects |url=https://erc.easme-web.eu/?p=757254 |website=erc.easme-web.eu}}<!-- auto-translated from Polish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> and an ERC Consolidator Grant in 2024<ref name=":0" />
